The reason is specific and measured rather than an excuse — /dev/kvm absent, adbd answering only after 113 minutes with no framework behind it, no GTK for a desktop stand-in, nothing faked from the PWA — and evidence/reliability.json partly stands in for it ('squeeze reached the host at intensity 0.62, the number it was sent at'; 177 events, gapless and in the same order on both sides, 0 duplicates). what_is_working: The iOS non-haptic substitute is real, and it is the strongest thing in this row. It is a whole-page translation, not a local animation: I cross-correlated the top standing-line strip against the bottom tab bar across all 421 frames of 07_feeling_landing.mp4 and they move together at r = 1.0000 with a maximum difference of 0.26 device pixels, horizontal component 0 everywhere.

The substitute is waveform-exact. Across eight arrivals in three clips (07 hold 0.90, squeeze 0.75, nuzzle 0.80, soup 0.85; 08 hold 0.92, squeeze 0.60, here 0.80, soup 0.70) the measured page-motion window matches the feeling's specified pattern length to within one 16 ms frame every time: 1888 vs 1900, 624 vs 640, 976 vs 990, 1184 vs 1200, 1888 vs 1900, 624 vs 640, 1984 vs 2000, 1184 vs 1200 ms.

It carries amplitude, not just rhythm. Peak displacement against the specified segment amplitude over the twelve segments of clip 07 gives r = 0.976, running from 9.0 device px (3.0 CSS px) at amplitude 90 to 23.9 device px (8.0 CSS px) at amplitude 230. Inside hold's 100 ms gap the page rings down 11.8 -> 8.4 -> 6.0 -> 4.2 -> 3.1 -> 2.1 device px rather than stopping dead, which is what a mass does.

It carries the sender's intensity. The same feeling at two intensities lands at the ratio the app's own report discloses: squeeze at 0.75 peaks at 23.9 device px and at 0.60 at 22.0 (1.086 measured against 1.093 predicted); soup at 0.55 peaks at 15.9 and at 0.90 at 19.1 (1.201 against 1.223). Both within two per cent.

The channel is reserved for feelings and nothing else. In 08_state_propagating.mp4 the sixteen frames after 'state mood restless' and the whole 140-frame message-and-unfold run show 0.00 device pixels of page motion, while every feeling run moves it. A message stays a message; only a feeling touches you.

The counts are met with room and are visible on screen rather than only in a log: 34 built-in feelings (36 total) across six named families, and the families appear as six paper tabs in the picker in 15_authored_feeling.mp4 — WARMTH, ACHE, SHELTER, MISCHIEF, STATIC, SPARKLE.

The patterns are well separated as designs. All 36 haptic strings, objects and sounds are distinct with no duplicates. On my own coarse test — pulse count, duration to the nearest 250 ms, mean on-amplitude to the nearest 40 of 255, and regular-versus-irregular — only 3 of 630 pairs collide (thinking of you / i'll make you tea, catch / yes, treat / pigeon), and each of those three still differs where a finger reads it: 300 ms gaps against 100 ms, 400 ms total against 620, the long pulse third against fourth.

The arrival is an object, not a coloured bubble. In 07 the hold stone travels across the partner's sheet casting a real shadow on the ruled paper before settling onto the desk shelf; in 08 the same feeling appears in the Chat thread as a modelled object resting on a torn slip. Nothing in the picker is an emoji: poke is a crumpled paper ball, snap a rubber band, stuck with me a row of staples, here a shallow bowl, it's okay a plaster.

Twelve partner-state signals are legible on one screen. 01_pulse.png shows MOOD, HERE, WHERE, NEED, ENERGY, BATTERY, LAST UP, THEIR CLOCK, RINGER, MOVING, SIGNAL, AT HOME as named fields plus the handwritten standing line; 01_pulse.report.json records 14 in the model.

At least four ambient presence surfaces, and the persistent one is live. The standing-line strip sits at the top of every region in every clip, and in 08 it changes from 'TRAVELLING NEED ||| ENERGY |' at frame 0 to 'OUT NEED ||| ENERGY |' at frame 638 after the far side sets place=out. The others are the Pulse partner sheet, the desk shelf of received feelings (also held at dusk in crops/dusk_pulse.png), the thread marginalia in Chat ('- noor is restless   Thu 3 Sep 19:40', 08 frames 180-280), and the composer's 'noor writing...'.

A feeling really is one gesture away from anywhere. The folded corner sits at the bottom right of nine of the ten stills — every region including Moments, Settings, Search and the media viewer — and is absent only from 10_first_run.png, which is before pairing. 15_authored_feeling.mp4 opens it on Us at frames 0-15 and on Pulse at frames 148-163 with the same fold, and frames 270-375 show a feeling landing while the reader is sitting in Settings.

05_settings.png gives the reader real control over what may reach them, in the app's own voice: fourteen kinds each set to wake me / quietly / not at all, with quiet hours 23:00 until 07:00, and no cheer, no badge and no streak anywhere in it.

The one fault frames.json flags on 08 is a capture seam, not the app. The brightness jump is a single frame: mean luma 154.9 at frame 304, 125.1 at 305, 156.9 at 306, and 304 is one of the recorded cuts_between_runs — the thread had scrolled to bare desk in the next take. The light in the app does not jump.
verdict: This row is carried by one thing done unusually well and undercut by one thing that cannot be shown here. The substitute the iOS PWA gets in place of a vibration is not a stand-in; it is engineered, and I could verify it against the specification without trusting a single builder number: the whole page translates as one body (top strip against tab bar, r = 1.0000, 0.26 device px apart at worst), the motion lasts exactly as long as the feeling's waveform in all eight arrivals I measured (never more than one 16 ms frame off), the displacement tracks the specified amplitude at r = 0.976 from 3.0 to 8.0 CSS px, the gaps ring down instead of stopping, the sender's intensity survives to within two per cent, and a message or a state change moves the page by 0.00 pixels — so the channel means one thing only. Around that, the counts are met with margin and visibly rather than in a log (34 built-ins, six paper family tabs, twelve named partner signals on one sheet, four ambient surfaces of which the persistent one demonstrably changes when the far side moves), the arrival is a modelled object casting a shadow on real paper rather than a bubble in another colour, the corner that reaches a feeling is in nine of ten stills, and the two authored feelings go through the picker, the send, the arrival, the waveform and the shelf on exactly the same rails as the built-ins. What is missing is the other half of the row's opening sentence and the far edge of its last clause. No gesture is shown anywhere: every intensity in the evidence is a number the harness typed, and frames 68-75 of clip 15 show the object leaving the grid with no press or force affordance at all. No device vibrated anywhere: the haptics are a specification, and the channel that was exercised is one a person can only see, so the row's own test — identifiable with the screen face down — is untestable here and, on the iPhone, unsatisfiable, since the sound that could have carried it is disclosed as mixed in over silence rather than recorded from the app. And the clause about being reached while the app is closed is evidenced on a Chromium desktop banner that the log itself disowns as neither an iPhone nor a lock screen, in words identical for all 36 feelings. The missing two-device frame is a real reason honestly given and partly answered by reliability.json, not an excuse. Seventeen: it clears the floor on the strength of the receiving end, and it clears it by exactly one clause's worth, because three of the nine things this row asks for are shown only as design rather than as behaviour.
